input: Source biodegradable packaging for my online orders

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The types of packaging needed (boxes, mailers, void fill, tape, labels) vary widely — knowing exactly which formats are required shapes the entire sourcing list.
Understanding what kind of products are being shipped (fragile, perishable, apparel, etc.) determines the protective requirements and which materials are appropriate.
Budget per unit or total spend directly limits which suppliers and material tiers are viable — premium compostable options cost significantly more than basic alternatives.
Order volume and frequency determine whether the user needs a wholesale supplier, a subscription, or a small one-off purchase — this changes sourcing strategy entirely.
The country or region affects which suppliers are accessible, shipping costs, import duties, and what certifications (e.g. EU OK Compost, USDA BioPreferred) are relevant.
The user may have a specific biodegradability standard in mind (home compostable vs. industrially compostable vs. recycled content) — this is a core filter for supplier selection.
Knowing whether the goal is to find a single supplier, compare multiple options, or actually place a first order defines what 'done' looks like and how far the plan needs to go.

gold.taskTitle: Source biodegradable packaging for online orders
gold.taskDescription: Find and procure biodegradable packaging materials suitable for fulfilling the user's online orders.

questions.title: Which packaging formats do you need to replace?
questions.description: Identify the specific packaging types required — e.g. shipping boxes, poly mailers, tissue paper, void fill, tape — to build a complete sourcing list.

questions.title: What kinds of products are you shipping to customers?
questions.description: Understand the nature of the products (fragile, soft goods, perishable, etc.) to determine the protective and structural requirements of the packaging.

questions.title: What is your target budget per unit or monthly spend?
questions.description: Establish a spend boundary to filter suppliers and material tiers — premium home-compostable options can cost 2-4x conventional packaging.

questions.title: How many orders do you ship per month on average?
questions.description: Determine order volume to decide whether wholesale, subscription, or small-batch sourcing is the right procurement model.

questions.title: Which country or region are you sourcing and shipping from?
questions.description: Pinpoint location to surface relevant local suppliers, certifications, and avoid high international shipping costs that would undermine sustainability goals.

questions.title: What biodegradability standard matters most to you?
questions.description: Clarify whether the priority is home compostable, industrially compostable, recycled content, or simply plastic-free — this is the primary filter for shortlisting materials.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like for this task?
questions.description: Determine the end goal — a shortlist of suppliers, a cost comparison, a sample order placed, or full transition complete — so the plan stops at the right point.
